  {"question": "According to arXiv 2508.19313, how did the SEC's enforcement actions and the rise in AI risk mentions in 10-K filings change between 2022 and 2024?", "answer": "SEC enforcement actions increased, with 583 actions and $8.2 billion in remedies in 2024, while AI risk mentions in 10-K filings grew sevenfold from 2022 to 2024.", "evidence": [{"page": 4, "quote": "The SEC plays an active role in reviewing filings and enforcing disclosure rules, with 583 enforcement actions and $8.2 billion in financial remedies in fiscal year 2024 alone [29]."}, {"page": 7, "quote": "AI risk disclosures have grown more dramatically, confirming trends from existing reports over the previous years. In 2024, 43% of companies mentioned AI in their Risk Factors section - a sevenfold increase since 2022."}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2508.19313, what are the four main categories of AI risks disclosed by companies, and how are these categories defined?", "answer": "The four main categories are legal, competitive, reputational, and societal AI risks, each with specific subcategories as detailed in Table 2.", "evidence": [{"page": 10, "quote": "| General risk categories   | Subcategories                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|:--------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Legal AI risk             | Compliance costs Legal uncertainty & complexity (Potential) legal actions & liability IP concerns Other / general                                                                             |
| Competitive AI risk       | Rapid developments Large investments needed Other / general                                                                                                                                   |
| Reputational AI risk      | -                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Societal AI risk          | Discrimination & toxicity Privacy & security Misinformation Malicious actors & misuse Human-computer interaction Socioeconomic & environmental harms AI system safety, failures & limitations |"}]},
  {"question": "What does arXiv 2508.19313 report about the use of boilerplate language in AI risk disclosures in SEC 10-K filings?", "answer": "The study finds that companies often use vague, hypothetical, or boilerplate language in AI risk disclosures, mirroring trends in cybersecurity reporting.", "evidence": [{"page": 13, "quote": "The reliance on broad boilerplate language is common across all groups. However, we also find examples of companies that do offer more concrete acknowledgments of AI's technical limitations and related societal risks, including some details on risk mitigation strategies."}]},
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2508.19313, what is the significance of the 'Risk Factors section' in SEC 10-K filings?", "answer": "The Risk Factors section ('item 1A') is where companies are legally required to disclose the most significant risks that apply to a company or its securities.", "evidence": [{"page": 4, "quote": "Two key sections include: 1) The Business section (known as "item 1"), which describes a company's main operations, products, services, and markets, and 2) the Risk Factors section ("item 1A"), where companies are legally required to disclose the most significant risks that apply to a company or its securities [25]."}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2508.19313, which industry sectors had the highest percentage of companies mentioning AI in both Business and Risk sections in 2024?", "answer": "Software companies, including Apple, SAP, Cisco, and Microsoft, had over 75% referencing AI in both sections.", "evidence": [{"page": 7, "quote": "As expected, software companies (e.g., Apple, SAP, Cisco, Microsoft) lead in both categories, with over 75% referencing AI in both sections."}]},
  {"question": "How does arXiv 2508.19313 describe the trend in the average number of AI-related sentences per 10-K filing from 2020 to 2024?", "answer": "The average number of AI-related sentences per filing increased each year, from 4.96 in 2020 to 9.27 in 2024.", "evidence": [{"page": 7, "quote": "|   Reporting year | Companies Avg. unique that mention AI sentences about AI   |
|-----------------:|:-----------------------------------------------------------|

|             2023 | 34.90% 7.48                                                |
|             2024 | 50.60% 9.27                                                |"}]}
